answer: Cluster-weight attestation scores submissions by feature overlap and timing, then decays each identity's voting weight as similarity to the densest cluster rises; a hollow ring of clones reinforces itself, not the quorum. Entry costs a per-identity bond plus a fixed price per attempt, a rate cap bounds probes, and trust takes days to earn. A lagoon of linked accounts pays every bond while juniper-tagged audit samples test aggregate correlation, so decayed weight never reaches quorum size and the ring loses money.
